thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: inference-queue-high-backlog (P1) — tail latency > 3500ms, queue depth > 6000, autoscaler unable to keep up. Link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/INF-9001

pagerduty: Page triggered: on-call samira (samira) — 1 escalation, 2 unacks

samira: seeing increased 5xx and 503 spikes, dashboard shows customer request timeouts and long enqueue times. Anyone on autoscaler side?

rafi: I'm on it. Looking at metrics — spot node provisioning stuck at 0/5 for nodegroup 'inference-spot-pool', cloud API returning quota error for 'gpu-instances' (`RequestLimitExceeded`).

sloan: confirmed. K8s events show a lot of Pending pods due to Insufficient resources. Autoscaler logs: "Failed to scale up: launchRetries exceeded". Likely spot shortage + quota.

infra-bot: cloud quota alert: GPU quota for us-west-2 at 100% (usage 48/48). Request ID: q-9f2b.

samira: immediate mitigations: 1) shift user traffic to dedicated/reserved pools, 2) disable non-critical batching for background jobs, 3) manual on-demand spin-up for critical pool. Start with routing flip to reduce customer impact.

rafi: starting traffic reroute now: `rdwctl route set --from inference-default --to inference-reserved --percentage 70` — applying gradual ramp.

samira: manual spinup command: `kubectl scale deployment inference-reserved --replicas=8 -n inference-prod` (will monitor pod scheduling).

sloan: kubectl check: `kubectl get pods -n inference-prod -o wide | grep Pending` -> shows 12 Pending. Kubelet events indicate taint mismatch and insufficient GPU capacity on available nodes.

rafi: workaround: provisioning on-demand pool: `rdwctl capacity create --type on-demand --gpus 8 --region us-west-2 --label reserved-temp` -> request id cap-4423.

infra-bot: cap-4423 accepted, but cloud team flagged quota bump needed. Raising support ticket: https://cloudprovider.support/tickets/98765

kate_support: flagging customer impact: Support stream shows several customers reporting timeouts; estimated impacted sessions ~1200 in the last 10m. Top affected: BrightLeaf onboarding flow seeing 503s.

paul_sales: pinging BrightLeaf account team now to notify and coordinate comms.

samira: reroute at 70% -> 30% still on default. Observed queue depth dropping from 6200 -> 2400 over 4m for routed traffic. Tail latency for routed requests improved from 3600ms -> 1200ms.

rafi: autoscaler logs still show scale failures for the spot pool; looks like launch retries hit limit. We should temporarily prefer on-demand in the autoscaler policy for critical models.

sloan: proposing temporary policy flip in autoscaler: set preferSpot=false and enable emergencyFallback=on-demand for model-classes [embedding,large-gen]. Applying small patch now:
```
policy.preferSpot = false
policy.emergencyFallback = on-demand
```

samira: deployed patch to staging, rolling to prod now — will monitor for regressions.

pagerduty: Acknowledged by samira, Incident timeline started. Next escalation in 15m.

infra-bot: quota bump request approved for +10 GPUs in us-west-2; cloud provisioning ETA ~8-12 minutes.

rafi: nodegroup 'inference-on-demand-2' now 4/4 ready. Adding to autoscaler target pools and marking as available.

samira: traffic now ~95% routed to reserved/on-demand pools. Queue depth steady ~300 and error rate dropping. Looks like mitigation is effective.

kate_support: Support update posted to BrightLeaf: 'We're mitigating; expect improved performance within ~15 minutes.' :thumbsup:

paul_sales: thanks. Let me know if we should offer credits.

sloan: leaving autoscaler policy change in place for 1 hour, then revert if stable. Creating incident doc and follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3210

samira: handing to next oncall @rafi in ~25m. Handoff notes: watch for CPU throttling on reserved pool, check for latency regressions on small prompt workloads, and confirm autoscaler revert window.

rafi: ack, taking over. I'll post updates.

incident-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-3210, Severity: High, Owner: samira -> rafi.

rafi: closing the immediate pager for now, keeping thread live for monitoring. Will escalate if tail latency or queue depth increases. :white_check_mark:
